result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the rubric well: deliberate, limited breaks; examples like the pull quote, full-bleed image and hero; and a strict surrounding grid so the break reads as intentional. B is broader, adding when not to break the grid and accessibility, but it has an editing slip: its 'Break by a meaningful amount' heading is followed by alignment advice, and it repeats the 'break decisively' point. A is tighter and gives more practical tests, such as changing more than just position, turning a repeated break into a grid rule, and checking narrow and long content. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover every rubric item well: deliberate and rare breaks, concrete examples, a consistent surrounding grid, and responsive testing. B is tighter and adds a useful practical point A lacks: change scale or treatment along with position, so a shifted element doesn't look misaligned. A has a mislabeled heading ('Break by a meaningful amount' actually describes anchoring) and some redundancy, though it does add accessibility and when-not-to guidance.
